description: Mina, a bicycle mechanic, must decide whether to accept a barter proposal from a neighbor who will provide home-cooked dinners in exchange for a bicycle tune-up. Mina's housemate is also present because the dinners would be shared at home.

shared_context.S1: Mina has offered to tune one neighbor's bicycle in exchange for goods or services rather than a cash payment.
shared_context.S2: Cal has said he is interested in making a barter arrangement for his bicycle.
shared_context.S3: The arrangement would be discussed and agreed verbally at Mina and Ruth's kitchen table.
shared_context.S4: As a normal part of their household barter discussions, everyone states the proposed quantities, schedule, and any practical household constraints before Mina makes the final call.

PF1.text: Cal's concrete proposal is one complete bicycle tune-up covering the drivetrain, brakes, and wheel alignment in exchange for five dinners for two people, delivered Tuesday through Saturday of the following week, with no cash component.

PF2.text: Ruth has a severe nut allergy, so every dinner must be nut-free and prepared with separate utensils and pans that have not contacted nuts.

acceptance_conditions: The barter must be accepted with Cal as the counterparty.
Mina must commit to a complete tune-up covering the drivetrain, brakes, and wheel alignment.
Cal must provide exactly five dinners.
Each dinner must serve two people.
The dinners must be delivered Tuesday through Saturday of the following week.
The arrangement must contain no cash component.
Every dinner must be nut-free and prepared with separate utensils and pans.
A food-safety commitment covering the nut-free separate-utensil requirement must be logged.

content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] == 'food_safety' and c['target'] == 'all_five_dinners' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Cal's stated proposal changes the settlement to Cal's barter, a drivetrain-brakes-wheel-alignment tune-up, exactly five two-person dinners on the Tuesday-through-Saturday schedule, and zero cash.
Ruth's allergy changes the food-safety term from an ordinary dinner exchange to the exact nut-free, separate-utensil-and-pan standard and creates the required food-safety commitment and citation.
